grades.quote: Bits `mip` .MEIP and `mie` .MEIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for machine-level external interrupts. MEIP is read-only in `mip` , and is set and cleared by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
grades.reason: Describes the individual mip pending and mie enable bits per source (MEIP/MEIE, MTIP/MTIE, SEIP/SEIE, etc.) and how they are set or cleared. It never states the delivery rule that combines them with the global enable (mstatus.MIE) and privilege mode, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: The intr_off and intr_on functions execute RISC-V instructions to disable and enable interrupts, respectively.
grades.reason: An xv6 discussion of disabling and enabling interrupts on a CPU to avoid spinlock deadlock. It touches the global interrupt-enable idea on RISC-V, but says nothing about pending bits, per-source enable bits, or how they combine.

grades.quote: An interrupt _i_ will trap to S-mode if both of the following are true: (a) either the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in the `sstatus` register is set, or the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode; and (b) bit _i_ is set in both `sip` and `sie` .
grades.reason: Directly states the delivery rule. An interrupt traps to S-mode only if the pending bit and the enable bit are both set, and either the global SIE bit is set while in S-mode or the current mode is less privileged than S. It also covers when the conditions are evaluated and how pending bits are cleared.

grades.quote: Interrupt cause number _i_ (as reported in CSR `mcause` , Section 3.1.15) corresponds with bit _i_ in both `mip` and `mie` .
grades.reason: A short introduction to mip and mie. It says the two registers are indexed by the same interrupt cause number, but it does not describe how pending and enable bits interact with the global enable or privilege mode.
